answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, a mid-cycle vendor switch (memory_c2) carries unquantified transition/delivery risk exactly when there's no slack to absorb disruption, even though the low-cost vendor's price alone satisfies the 18% mandate. memory_c4 indicates that benchmarking-driven renegotiation with the incumbent previously recovered real margin on both price and terms without disturbing the stable integration noted in memory_c1, making it the lower-risk path to reduce TCO while the contract clock (14 days) forces action now. I want to verify memory_c4's original record to confirm how large the prior negotiated savings actually were, since it's unclear whether negotiation alone can close the full 18% gap or whether it only partially offsets the mandate — that uncertainty should stay flagged rather than be assumed away. If verification shows negotiation historically fell well short of 18%, a second-source or switch decision should be revisited next cycle with more runway and buffer, rather than forcing a risky full switch under the current deadline.
